title: plugin-charts: recharts' tick-size measurement span inherits document.body's font, not the chart's — fontFamily mismatch silently mis-measures tick overlap
body:
## 维护者速读

我们的图表在坐标轴标签太挤时会自动隐藏一部分。要决定隐藏哪些,得先量每个标签有多宽 —— 而我们用的图表库
**是用整个页面的字体去量的,不是用图表自己的字体**。字体不一样,量出来就不对:该隐藏的没隐藏(标签叠在
一起),或者不该隐藏的被隐藏了(数据点从轴上消失)。我们自己已经有一个组件中招:它的纵轴用等宽字体显示,
却按页面字体在量。

三条路:**A** 只写进文档、同时把修复提给上游图表库(我们这边不动代码,问题还在,但被记下来了);
**B** 用一个能奏效但没有文档支持的写法绕过去 —— 实测它会**顺带改变同一个页面上其它图表**的标签密度,
包括不是我们做的图表;**C** 当作上游的限制,关掉这张卡。

请裁一个字母:**A / B / C**?

os-decision-facets

- **① 项目长远合理性**:A 缩小特例(把问题留在它真正所属的上游),B **扩大**特例 —— 它要求把「inline style 只开给颜色」这条唯一的 carve-out 撕开一个非颜色的口子,并让我们永久依赖第三方两个没有文档的内部行为(一份共享的测量元素、以及它不会清除已写入的字段)。
- **② 实际业务拉动**:今天就有人撞上 —— 已发布的 `@object-ui/plugin-charts` 里 `ChartImpl` 的纵轴正按错字体被测量(执行席在源上确认:它写 `fontFamily: 'monospace'` 且没有 `interval` 属性,默认 `preserveEnd` ⇒ 宽度要被量)。⇒ 非零拉动,⛔ 不适用 defer 默认。
- **③ 防 AI 犯错**:这条缺陷是**静默**的 —— 没有报错、没有红门禁,只是标签数量悄悄不对。A 把它写成一句明文约束(宿主页面字体须与图表字体一致),⇒ 从「静默泄露」变成「写下来的前提」;B 则再加一层静默:它的纠正发生在第二次测量、且会溢出到别的图表,而本包的测试环境对所有字符串返回零宽度,任何单测都看不见。
- **④ 创业阶段不扩散**:A 不新增任何已声明的键与永久义务;B 每加一处 pin 就是一处永久义务,且其正确性由第三方的未文档行为兜底 —— 上游一次改版即失效,而失效的表现仍然是**静默**的。

Prior rulings read: colour-bearing,no inline styles,font-family,recharts → objectui `AGENTS.md:30`/`:37` + `skills/objectui/rules/styling.md:3`–`:5`(inline style 禁令与其**仅限颜色**的唯一 carve-out);`docs/adr` 0 hits;⛔ 与 recharts 测量本身有关的裁决:none

推荐 **A**,回退 **C**。⛔ 不荐 B:它的溢出是**实测**的,不是推测,受害者包含我们不拥有的图表。
自检:**只看①选 A;②③④ 是否翻转:否** —— ② 的真实拉动让人想立刻动手(倾向 B),但 ③ 与 ④ 指出 B 的修复
本身是静默且会溢出的 ⇒ 不翻字母,只把 ② 变成 A 里「同时提上游」的紧迫性。
置信缺口:⛔ 执行席**没有**独立复跑那次 Chromium 溢出实验,只复核了它的前提与仓内实例;⛔ 也没量过今天有
多少已发布图表实际处在字体不一致的页面上。

⛔ 正文原文一字未动,全部保留在下方。</sub>

---

## What

Found while verifying objectui#7386 (`packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`, the `xAxisCommonProps` categorical-axis `minTickGap` fix) in real Chromium.

Recharts measures each axis tick label's pixel size via a hidden `span` element
(`getStringSize` / `measureTextWithDOM` in `recharts/es6/util/DOMUtils.js`)
that is appended directly to `document.body`:

```js
var measurementSpan = document.createElement('span');
...
document.body.appendChild(measurementSpan);
```

`CartesianAxis` (`recharts/es6/cartesian/CartesianAxis.js`) does correct
`fontSize` and `letterSpacing` after mount, by reading
`window.getComputedStyle()` on the FIRST already-rendered real tick and
feeding that back into the next measurement pass:

```js
var calculatedFontSize = computedStyle.fontSize;
var calculatedLetterSpacing = computedStyle.letterSpacing;
```

It never reads or corrects `fontFamily`. So the hidden measurement span is
styled with whatever `document.body` computes its font-family to — NOT the
font-family actually applied to the chart's own tick text (in this repo,
`ChartContainerImpl`'s `text-xs` wrapper class plus whatever `body { }` rule
is in scope). When those two differ, `getStringSize` measures every tick
label using the WRONG font's glyph widths, and every downstream decision that
depends on it — `minTickGap`-based thinning, angled-tick collision avoidance
(`getAngledRectangleWidth`), `interval: 'preserveStartEnd'`'s boundary math —
is silently computed off a wrong number. It can go either way: if the wrong
font is narrower than the real one, recharts under-thins and labels visually
overlap; if wider, it over-thins and drops labels that would have fit.

## Repro (measured)

A minimal real-Chromium harness (React + recharts 3.10.1, no
`ChartContainerImpl`, no CSS at all — so `document.body`'s font-family is the
Times New Roman UA default) rendering a plain `<BarChart>` with an `<XAxis>`
whose rendered tick text was explicitly given `font-family: system-ui,
sans-serif` via a wrapper `className`:

```
tick element computed font-family:            system-ui, sans-serif
#recharts_measurement_span computed font-family: "Times New Roman"
```

With that mismatch in place, a rotated-rectangle overlap check (SAT, using
each tick's real `getCTM()`-mapped corners — not an axis-aligned
`getBoundingClientRect()`, which over-reports collisions for diagonal text)
found real, visible overlapping labels at `minTickGap: 0` for several
bucket-count / width combinations. Re-running the SAME harness after adding a
`body { font-family: ... }` rule matching `apps/console/src/index.css`'s
actual rule (so the hidden span's inherited font now matches the tick's) made
every one of those overlaps disappear — screenshots confirmed no visible
overlap either way once the fonts matched.

## Why this repo does not currently see it

`apps/console/src/index.css` sets `body { font-family: -apple-system, "SF Pro
Text", ..., system-ui, sans-serif, ... }`, and `ChartContainerImpl`'s
`text-xs` wrapper class does not override `font-family` — so today, inside
this repo's own console app, `document.body`'s font-family happens to match
what the chart tree actually renders with, and the mismatch this issue
describes does not manifest.

## Why it is still real

`@object-ui/plugin-charts` is a published package other consumers embed. Any
host page whose `body` font-family differs from the font the chart container
ends up rendering with (a different global font stack, a modal/iframe with
scoped styles, a design system that sets font-family lower than `body`, or
simply a consumer that never sets a body font at all) gets silently wrong
tick-density and collision decisions from recharts, with no error, warning,
or test able to catch it (this repo's own DOM test environment reports zero
text metrics for every string, so unit tests cannot observe this dimension
either — real-Chromium verification is required, same limitation objectui#7386
documents for its own fix).

## Where

Not fixable inside recharts from here (its `CartesianAxis`'s font-size
correction effect is the one place this would need to also read and pass
`fontFamily`, and that is upstream code). The place ObjectUI could act is
`packages/plugin-charts/src/ChartContainerImpl.tsx` / `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`:
neither currently passes an explicit `tick={{ fontFamily: ... }}` (or
equivalent) to any `<XAxis>` / `<YAxis>`, which would give recharts a
font-family it does not need to (and currently cannot) discover via
`computedStyle` on the wrong element.

## Note

This is a **product judgement**, not a mechanical one — it involves deciding
whether ObjectUI should defensively pin a font-family for tick measurement
(and if so, read from where: the resolved CSS custom property, a hardcoded
match to `text-xs`'s stack, or something else), or accept the latent risk as
a recharts limitation and document it for consumers. Filed unassigned for
triage rather than carried into objectui#7386, whose scope is the
`minTickGap` value on the `>5 bucket` branch specifically.
